text:
alex: ran a focused nsys trace on node-gpu-03 after the kernel-selector change (prefers cutlass_fp16 for <=64). seeing a long tail in P50->P99 for short sequences, looks like kernel launch / enqueue overhead piling up
maya: can you attach the trace? is this only on nv0 or across the pool?
alex: upload here: https://perf-storage.internal/nsys/1805123456.nsys.json (nv0 only so far)
perf-bot: nsys trace processed: timeline + kernel table available at https://perf-ui.internal/trace/1805123456
jordan: quick look: timeline shows many very short matmul kernels (~5-8us) interleaved with 10-20us gaps. total per-token time dominated by enqueue latency for these small GEMMs.
maya: that matches suspicion. kernel-selector is switching to cutlass_fp16 microkernel which has lower FLOPS for tiny sizes but more launches. what does KV cache timeline say? any memcpy spikes?
alex: KV cache mostly happy, but I see periodic memcpy of ~40-60us right before a burst of mats. looks like cache sweep + prefetch + tiny matmuls. snippet from trace: ```
Kernel 1234: cutlass_gemm_fp16 (size 16x32) 6.2us
Memcpy HtoD 345: 48.1us
Kernel 1235: cutlass_gemm_fp16 (size 8x16) 5.4us
```
pri ya: (typo) priya: hmm, could be small-batch scheduling combined with continuous batching window being too short. if we open the window slightly we can aggregate more tokens into a single matmul -> bigger kernels -> fewer launches.
jordan: also check our kernel fallback policy: when sequence_len <= 64 we prefer cutlass_fp16, otherwise cuBLAS_lt. maybe the selector isn't considering batch_size distribution. recent change removed weighting by batch_size.
maya: that was the regression. revert or refine selector to factor in batch_shape.
alex: ran an A/B experiment: disabled cutlass preference for short sequences on a small fleet. P50 unchanged but P95/P99 dropped 18-22%. attaching before/after perf counters: ```
before: avg_kernel_launches_per_token=0.6, avg_enqueue_gap=12.4us, p99_latency=112ms
after: avg_kernel_launches_per_token=0.18, avg_enqueue_gap=3.2us, p99_latency=88ms
```
perf-bot: perf regression alert suppressed for that fleet after change (tag: runtime-hotfix-180512).
priya: aside from selector, we should consider merging tiny matmuls into batched GEMM path in runtime (continuous-batching aggregator). that would reduce kernel-launch overhead without losing cache locality. tradeoff: increases code complexity and memory copies.
jordan: agreed. another option: increase continuous batching window from 6ms -> 12ms for short sequences only. that should increase batch_size without affecting tail for long queries.
maya: let's do two quick follow-ups: 1) revert selector patch to previous weighting by batch_size (alex), 2) run nsys with nvprof-style counters to capture SM occupancy and warps for small matmuls (jordan). prioritize 1 today.
alex: started rollback PR, will push in 15m. also flagged the rollback in deploy-bot.
jordan: I'll queue an nsys job with occupancy counters and run a perfetto capture on host side to see scheduling gaps.
maya: nice. if rollback fixes P99 we can plan a smarter selector that models batch_size distribution + kv-cache memcpy cost. create an RFC in eng-runtime outlining metrics and tests.
priya: I'll take the RFC, include proposed continuous-batching changes and memory-copy tradeoffs.
alex: thanks all — leaving the trace links + a short perf note in the incident kanban. we can close this thread after post-rollback verification (target EOD). :thumbsup:
